correctness.rationale: Direct incidence counts give the full powered-distance block matrix. The strongly regular point graph has nontrivial incidence squared singular values s+t or 0. Each paired sector is strictly negative for p in [0,1] by b-1<=2(a-1) and a^2>=4(a-1); the singular-zero sectors are strictly negative below p0=log2(1+1/max{s,t}). The explicit point-line contrast quadratic form equals F_{s,t}(p)/((s+1)(t+1)(st+1)). Writing a=2^p and gamma=log2 3, f(a)=Aa+Ba^2-Ca^gamma-D is strictly increasing because 2B-C=2st(st-1)>0 and f'(1)>0; the Taylor bound proves f(1+1/max{s,t})>0. The unique root lies before every competing sector, giving the necessary and sufficient exponent and the sole endpoint zero mode. value.rationale: A natural infinite class of thick generalized-quadrangle Levi graph metrics acquires an exact optimal Gaussian-kernel exponent depending only on (s,t), despite potentially many nonisomorphic incidence geometries. The proof separates the bipartition contrast from nonconstant incidence harmonics and shows a sharp one-dimensional embedding-rank transition. In contrast with complete designs and projective incidence graphs, the diameter-four partial geometry produces a new explicit four-scale root equation and a stable contrast-dominance mechanism.
